gloss: A deep realm associated with the dead or the confinement of evil spirits.
note: Romans 10 uses it in speaking of bringing Christ up from the dead.

gloss: Being received into a family with the standing of a son or daughter.
note: Paul applies this to belonging to God's family; it does not imply physical birth.

gloss: Sexual unfaithfulness that breaks a marriage commitment.
note: Also used as a picture of unfaithfulness to God.

gloss: A structure on which offerings are presented to God or to a god.
note: An altar can serve true worship or false worship.

gloss: Truly, or let it be so.
note: Used to affirm a statement or prayer; Revelation also uses it as a title.

gloss: A heavenly messenger or servant of God.
note: Some passages describe fallen angels; the word does not mean a person becomes an angel after death.

gloss: Marked with oil or set apart for a particular role.
note: Can mean ordinary application of oil or consecration; anointing eyes with mud is physical application.

gloss: A messenger sent with authority, especially someone commissioned by Jesus.
note: The title concerns a commission, not simply any follower.

gloss: Dealing with sin and guilt so a relationship with God can be restored.
note: The BSB uses atoning sacrifice, not propitiation; this gloss does not choose one atonement theory.

gloss: A washing with water marking repentance or identification with Jesus.
note: The BSB also speaks of baptism with the Spirit and figurative baptism into suffering.

gloss: Speech that insults God or dishonors what belongs to Him.
note: An accusation of blasphemy does not mean the accused person actually committed it.

gloss: Favored with good, spoken well of, or worthy of praise.
note: Can mean God's favor, a person's blessing, praising God, or even misguided human praise.

gloss: Given a new beginning and life through God's Spirit.
note: John 3 contrasts this with physical birth; no particular account of baptism is assumed.

gloss: Jesus' description of Himself as the one who gives true life.
note: Retained despite two BSB verses because the phrase is central to John 6.

gloss: Summoned, invited, or named, depending on the passage.
note: Can mean God's summons, calling out, naming, or describing someone; not every call is election.

gloss: Heavenly beings associated with God's presence, also represented in sanctuary artwork.
note: The singular is cherub; the BSB also describes carved representations.

gloss: The Messiah, God's anointed one.
note: A title, not Jesus' surname; Messiah and Christ express the same title.

gloss: Removal of the foreskin, given to Abraham as a sign of God's covenant.
note: Also used figuratively for the heart; uncircumcision is kept as a separate, opposite term.

gloss: Free from dirt, moral wrongdoing, or ritual restrictions, as the passage specifies.
note: Ritual cleanness concerns eligibility for worship or permitted use, not simply hygiene or sinlessness.

gloss: An instruction given with authority, especially by God.
A verdict declaring someone guilty and liable to punishment.
note: Can describe divine or human verdicts; a denial of condemnation still uses the term.

gloss: To acknowledge openly what is true, including sin or faith in Jesus.
note: Can mean admitting wrongdoing or declaring belief, not only a private religious practice.

gloss: A binding commitment that establishes a relationship and its promises or duties.
To desire something belonging to someone else in a wrongful way.
note: Not every desire is coveting.

gloss: Counted to someone's account or regarded as theirs.
note: An accounting word used for righteousness in Romans 4; may concern ordinary financial credit elsewhere.

gloss: Put to death on a cross.
note: Also used figuratively for the believer's old self or sinful desires.

gloss: A declaration or wish that harm or judgment will fall on someone or something.
note: Can mean God's judgment, hostile human speech, or abusive language.

gloss: An evil spiritual being opposed to God.
note: An accusation of having a demon need not be true; demon-possessed is a compound adjective.

gloss: A learner who follows a teacher and their teaching.
note: Can describe followers of Jesus, John, Moses, or other teachers.

gloss: Chosen for a particular purpose or relationship.
note: May describe God's choosing or ordinary human choices; no theory of election is assumed.

gloss: Life with God that never ends, given through Jesus.
Trust or belief, especially trust in God and His promises.
note: Can describe personal trust or the shared belief Christians hold; faithful has its own entry.

gloss: Being trustworthy and keeping promises.
note: Can describe God or people; it is distinct from having faith.

gloss: The child born first, or someone holding the firstborn's special rank and rights.
note: Can describe birth order or supreme rank; read the surrounding passage.

gloss: The first part of a harvest, offered to God or pointing to more to come.
note: Also used figuratively for people, the Spirit, or resurrection.

gloss: The body, human kinship or weakness, or human nature opposed to God.
note: Genesis 2 concerns bodily kinship; Romans 8 contrasts flesh with the Spirit; Jesus truly became flesh.

gloss: Knew beforehand.
note: God's prior knowledge is stated without deciding among Christian accounts of its meaning.

gloss: To release someone from guilt or a debt rather than hold it against them.
note: Can concern sins or debts; forgiveness does not say the wrongdoing was acceptable.

gloss: A person belonging to a nation other than Israel.
note: A covenant identity term, not a list of people; Gentile does not simply mean unbeliever.

gloss: Given glory or shown to be worthy of honor.
note: Can mean honoring God or receiving glory; not identical to the noun glory.

gloss: Greatness, beauty, and honor made known or recognized.
note: May describe God's majesty, human honor, or the honor God shares with His people.

gloss: Living in devotion to God.
note: Different from being God; it describes devotion and conduct.

gloss: The good news of God's saving work through Jesus Christ.
note: Good news can also mean ordinary welcome news; identify its sense from the passage.

gloss: God's freely given kindness and help, which people cannot earn.
The realm of the dead in New Testament language.
note: Do not collapse Hades, the lake of fire, and the Abyss into one term.

gloss: To become, or make someone, stubborn and unwilling to listen.
note: May describe hearts, people, or physical things; the passage identifies who acts.

gloss: The chief priest who represents the people before God.
note: In Israel the high priest had special worship duties; Hebrews applies the title to Jesus.

gloss: Set apart for God, who is completely pure and unlike all others.
Expectation or trust directed toward something still to come.
note: May mean ordinary expectation or confident trust in God's promise.

gloss: Images or other things treated as gods or given worship owed to God.
note: Includes false worship; not every image is an idol.

gloss: Life that is not subject to death.
What someone receives as an heir, including what God promises His people.
note: Can mean family property, land, or blessings God promises.

gloss: Serious wrongdoing or the guilt it brings.
Speaks or appeals on someone else's behalf.
note: Can concern the Spirit, Christ, or people appealing for others.

gloss: A decision about right and wrong, including the outcome God declares.
note: Can mean God's verdict, human decisions, or commands; do not assume every use means punishment.

gloss: Put in right standing with God.
note: God puts people in right standing with Himself; other passages use justify for proving a claim right.

gloss: God's rule and the life of those who belong under His reign.
note: Kingdom of heaven is a related BSB expression; neither simply means a geographical place.

gloss: John's title for Jesus, who takes away the world's sin.
note: Retained despite two BSB verses because this title is central to John 1.

gloss: An authoritative instruction or rule, often God's teaching given through Moses.
note: Can mean Moses' Law, Scripture more broadly, a civil rule, or a working principle.

gloss: Disregard for God's law or rightful authority.
note: Lawless acts are a phrase using the adjective, not a form of the word law.

gloss: Fresh flowing water, used by Jesus as a picture of the life God gives.
note: Can mean literal flowing water; John 7 explicitly connects Jesus' picture with the Spirit.

gloss: Steady, faithful love that does not give up on its commitments.
Food God provided for Israel in the wilderness.
note: John 6 contrasts manna eaten by Israel's ancestors with Jesus, the bread of life.

gloss: Compassion shown to someone in need or deserving punishment.
Something presented to God in worship.
note: Can concern true or false worship; ordinary acts of offering have a wider meaning.

gloss: An ancestral father of a family or people, especially Israel's early ancestors.
Wholeness, well-being, or the end of hostility.
note: Can describe peace with God, peace between people, personal well-being, or absence of war.

gloss: Decided beforehand by God.
note: The gloss does not settle how God's purpose relates to human choice.

gloss: A person appointed to serve in worship and present offerings for others.
note: Includes priests of Israel, priests of other gods, and figurative priesthood.

gloss: A commitment to do or give what has been said.
note: May be God's commitment or a human promise.

gloss: Someone who speaks a message from God.
note: Can include false claimants; prophecy is the message or activity, not merely predicting the future.

gloss: The removal of what makes a person or object unclean.
note: May concern ritual cleanness or moral purification.

gloss: The price paid to set someone free.
note: Do not assume a recipient of the ransom where the passage names none.

gloss: Brought back into a peaceful relationship after being enemies or separated.
Bought back or set free at a cost.
note: Can concern property, release from slavery, or God's saving work.

gloss: The smaller group left after others are lost, scattered, or judged.
note: Can also describe what remains of objects or nations, without implying faithfulness.

gloss: To turn away from wrongdoing and turn toward God.
note: Regretting wrongdoing alone is not the whole meaning of repentance.

gloss: Being raised from death to life.
note: The passage identifies whose resurrection is meant and whether life or judgment follows.

gloss: Being right before God or acting in ways that are right in His sight.
note: Can describe God's justice, right conduct, or standing before Him; keep the passage's distinction.

gloss: The seventh day set apart for rest and worship.
An offering given to God, often involving an animal's death.
note: Also used figuratively for devotion or service and of offerings to false gods.

gloss: People set apart as belonging to God.
note: In these biblical uses this is not limited to people later formally recognized by a church.

gloss: Rescue from danger or from sin and its consequences.
note: Can mean physical deliverance or God's saving work; not every saved thing concerns eternal life.

gloss: Set apart for God and His purposes.
note: Can concern people, objects, or days; the context may emphasize growth in holiness.

gloss: A mark that confirms ownership, authority, or that something is genuine.
note: Also a device or closure; Romans 4 uses it for circumcision confirming righteousness by faith.

gloss: The realm of the dead, often pictured as the depths below.
note: An Old Testament term; do not automatically equate every use with final punishment.

gloss: Doing, wanting, or failing to do what goes against God's will.
note: Can describe particular wrongs or sin as a ruling power; sin offerings are ritual uses.

gloss: A title identifying Jesus' unique relationship with God the Father.
note: Plural sons of God has other contexts: heavenly beings or people belonging to God.

gloss: A human being; also Jesus' title for Himself, echoing Daniel's vision.
note: Psalm 8 uses the phrase for humanity; Jesus' title must be read in its own context.

gloss: A living person or their inner life.
note: Can refer to the whole person, life itself, or the inward self; avoid imposing one body-soul theory.

gloss: God's Spirit, a person's inner life, or a spiritual being, depending on context.
note: Capitalization and context distinguish God's Spirit from human spirits and other spiritual beings.

gloss: A tent or dwelling, especially Israel's portable sanctuary for worship.
note: Plural Tabernacles can name the feast of shelters; do not confuse it with the sanctuary.

gloss: A sacred building used for worship.
note: Can mean God's temple or a pagan temple; also used for Jesus' body and God's people.

gloss: Breaking a command or crossing a boundary God has set.
A wrongdoing that violates a duty or God's command.
note: Often overlaps sin and transgression; it does not only mean entering another person's land.

gloss: The state of not being circumcised.
note: Can describe physical status or figuratively an unresponsive heart or ears.

gloss: Defiled or not permitted for holy use under the passage's requirements.
note: Ritual uncleanness is not automatically moral guilt; unclean spirits are another use.

gloss: Without reverence for God or opposed to His ways.
note: The opposite of godly; not a form of godliness.

gloss: Being or acting against what is right in God's sight.
note: Opposite of righteousness; never count these forms as righteousness.

gloss: A covering or curtain that conceals or separates.
note: Can mean a face covering, a sanctuary curtain, or a figurative barrier to understanding.

gloss: Serious moral evil expressed in a person's desires or actions.
A spoken message; as Jesus' title, God's self-expression made known in Him.
note: Usually ordinary speech or God's message; John 1 uses Word as a title for Jesus.

gloss: Actions people do, including deeds considered in relation to God's law and faith.
note: Can also describe God's acts, miracles, or ordinary work; it is not always earning salvation.

gloss: Deep anger, especially God's just anger against evil.
